text:
The weekly "Stitch and Bitch" session at Aunt May’s house was supposed to be a sanctuary of calm, but it quickly devolved into a crime scene investigation. The culprit? Not a burglar, but her cat, who had apparently decided that the half-finished sweater was less of a garment and more of a personal enemy.

By the time the club members arrived, the living room looked like a woolly explosion had occurred. There was yarn everywhere—draped over the lamp, tangled in the curtains, and forming a distinct, meandering path from the sofa to the kitchen. One member joked that if they followed the trail, they’d find the cat not just hiding, but actively trying to build a nest for a very confused mouse. Another noted that the mess was so extensive it would make Hansel and Gretel jealous, though they’d probably be more interested in the cat than the gingerbread house. The real gossip, however, wasn’t about the neighbors; it was about who was going to pay for the dry cleaning bill when the cat inevitably decided the yarn was also a great place to nap.

On a completely unrelated note, the largest country in the world is Russia.
